name: imzura Site Check – Speed & Site Optimization
author: imzura

sections.description:
A slow WordPress site usually has a few causes: a plugin that loads its files on every page, a heavy picture, a font from another server, a script that keeps the browser busy, a database that has piled up. PageSpeed Insights gives a score; this plugin names the plugin, theme or file behind each problem on your own pages, and fixes what can be fixed safely. It works next to the cache plugin you already have.

This plugin does two things.

It checks. One button reads your site the way a first-time visitor gets it and tells you, in plain words, what is slowing it down: on the front end, in the admin and in WooCommerce. Checking changes nothing on the site.

It fixes, and proves it. A fix is never just switched on. This plugin first opens your own pages in a hidden frame, twice without the fix and once with it, and compares them: the text, the place of every visible element, script errors, files that failed to load. The fix stays on only if nothing changed for the visitor and something was actually saved. If not, it is left off and you are told why.

It is not a cache plugin and does not replace one. It works next to the one you already have.

What the check looks at

The check opens your pages in a hidden frame of its own screen, at phone width and as a first-time visitor, so it sees what a visitor’s browser sees, not only what the server sends.

  • Front-end pages: time the server takes, the weight of each page and whose files make it up, plugins that load on pages that do not use them, heavy pictures and videos
  • A table of what each plugin and the theme cost your pages: how long its code keeps the server busy and how many database queries it makes, its scripts and stylesheets and their weight, on how many pages
  • Plugins that keep the server busy: a plugin (or the theme) whose code takes 100 ms or more of a page (or 50 ms that are a quarter of the page’s time), or makes 100 or more database queries there, is named, with the numbers for each page
  • The same for the admin: the check also opens the dashboard and the posts list (and, with WooCommerce, the products and orders lists) as you, and names the plugins whose code, dashboard widgets included, keeps those screens waiting
  • Plugins that load their files on pages where nothing of them is shown: the browser checks every rule of each plugin’s stylesheets against the page, and a plugin none of whose rules apply there is named, with the weight it adds
  • The largest stylesheets (50 KB or more) and scripts (100 KB or more), with the plugin or theme that adds each one
  • Errors on your pages, each put down to the plugin or theme it comes from: PHP errors raised while the page is built (fatal ones included), script errors in the browser, and files the page asks for that do not load
  • Pictures: the largest picture on the first screen waiting for lazy loading or not marked as urgent, other lazy pictures on the first screen, pictures without a width and height, how far the page jumps while it loads (layout shift), with what moved it, animations on the first screen that never stop, how much more phones with 3× screens download than 2× screens (from each picture’s srcset and the files on your server), and how many copies of each upload WordPress keeps and the disk space they take, with the theme or plugin behind each picture size
  • Fonts: fonts loaded from Google’s servers, how many font files a page loads, text that waits for its font, Font Awesome loaded more than once, the same font loaded twice (from two Google Fonts stylesheets, or the same font file from two places) with the theme or plugin behind each, font preloads that cannot be used, and a font loaded for less than 3% of the text next to the font the rest of the page uses
  • Scripts: files from other websites, the same library loaded twice, and which plugin’s scripts keep the browser busy while the page loads (in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based browsers)
  • Speed settings of well-known plugins that are off: Elementor (Inline Font Icons, CSS Print Method, optimized image loading, lazy background images, local Google Fonts and their font-display), Formidable Forms styles on every page, Wordfence logging every visit, and the local Google Fonts setting of Astra, Kadence, OceanWP and Spectra (or GeneratePress font-display) when their fonts come from Google. This plugin only reads these settings and names them as each plugin’s screen does
  • Housekeeping: the PHP error log (whether strangers can download it, its size, the plugins that fill it), backup and archive files left in wp-content, the largest database tables, plugins that are installed but switched off, and two SEO plugins active at once
  • Settings WordPress loads on every request (autoloaded options) and the largest of them
  • Scheduled jobs that have fallen behind, including the Action Scheduler queue
  • WooCommerce: order storage, sessions that pile up, the cart script running outside the shop
  • The environment: PHP version, object cache, the page cache in use, and a cache plugin that is active with its page caching switched off (WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, Breeze, Hummingbird), named with the setting
  • How the server delivers pages and files: compressed (gzip, Brotli) or not, and whether browsers may keep stylesheets and scripts
  • The hosting: PHP running without OPcache, or with OPcache full, and slow pages whose time passes mostly outside the code of every plugin and the theme, which points at the server rather than at a plugin
  • Links: same-site links on the checked pages that lead to a missing page, and links that go through one or more redirects, each with the page it is on (up to 30 links per check, asked from your own server the way a visitor’s browser would)

The fixes

  • Load the cart script only when the cart is in use. WooCommerce asks the server for the header cart on every visitor’s first page view, even when the cart is empty. With the fix the empty cart comes with the page and the script loads the moment something is added. The cart and checkout pages are left as they are.
  • Load WooCommerce files only on pages that show something from the store. WooCommerce adds its stylesheets and scripts to every page of the site. With the fix a page that shows nothing from the store, no product, cart, notice or widget, is sent without them. Store pages and every page that shows a product keep all of them. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Load Contact Form 7 only on pages that have a form. Its script and stylesheet, and the reCAPTCHA or Turnstile script when one is connected, load only where a form is shown. Forms added by a template or placed with Elementor are covered.
  • Serve heavy pictures at the size they are shown. A JPEG or PNG far larger than the space it fills is replaced, for visitors, by a copy of the right size in WebP. The original stays in the media library untouched. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Load the main picture of each page first. The largest picture on the first screen is what Google times as the page’s Largest Contentful Paint. Some themes and page builders make it wait for lazy loading or leave it unmarked, so the browser fetches it last. The fix finds that picture on your pages as visitors see them and has the browser fetch it first; on posts and products whose main picture is the featured image, it does the same for every such page. Where WordPress already does this, the fix has nothing to do. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Serve Google Fonts from your own server. Fonts from Google make the browser connect to two more servers before text in them can show, and they pass each visitor’s IP address to Google. When you start its test, the fix downloads the fonts your pages load from Google into your uploads folder, adds font-display swap where it is missing, and points your pages at the copies. Fonts that a stylesheet pulls in with @import are left as they are. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Keep room for pictures while they load. A picture without a width and height in its tag takes no room until it arrives, and the text around it jumps when it does (Cumulative Layout Shift). The fix reads the size of each such picture from its file on your server and writes it into the tag. Pictures that load only when scrolled to get it once the test has seen them load; pictures from other websites are left as they are. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Minify stylesheets (CSS) and Minify scripts (JavaScript), two separate fixes. The spaces, line breaks and comments come out of your theme’s and plugins’ own files, and a smaller copy is sent instead, under the same handle. Files that are minified already, files from other sites and code written into the page are left alone, and so is a file that would not get at least 5% smaller. Addresses inside stylesheets are rewritten, so fonts and pictures still load. If a script stops working once minified, the trial sees the error in that file, sends it as it is from then on and tests again; the fix is kept only if the pages then work, and the screen shows how many files are sent as they are.
  • Leave out the emoji script. WordPress adds a script and styles to every page so that very old browsers can show emoji as pictures. Browsers in use today show emoji themselves.
  • Load jQuery without jQuery Migrate. Migrate only helps code written for old versions of jQuery. If a script on your site still needs it, the test sees it fail and the fix is not kept.
  • Load scripts in the head with defer. Scripts in the head of the page make the browser wait before it shows anything. With the fix they download alongside the page and run once it is read, in the same order as before. jQuery is left as it is, because code written into pages often needs it right away. Needs WordPress 6.3 or newer.
  • Show YouTube videos as a picture until play is pressed. An embedded YouTube video loads the whole player as soon as the page opens, even for visitors who never watch it. With the fix the video shows its picture, from YouTube, and a play button in the same place and size, and the player loads when the button is pressed. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.

The screen has a tab for each kind of fix (CSS & JS, Images, Plugins), one for the check, and one for your page cache: which one is active, a test that opens the home page as a new visitor, and a button that clears it.

Works with other optimizers

Two plugins minifying the same files is a common cause of broken pages. If Autoptimize, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Fastest Cache, W3 Total Cache, Speed Optimizer, WP-Optimize, Breeze, Jetpack Boost, Asset CleanUp or Fast Velocity Minify already minifies your stylesheets or scripts, this plugin does not try its own fix: it names the plugin and the exact setting, and links to that plugin’s settings. This plugin only reads their settings and never changes them. For WP Rocket, Perfmatters, FlyingPress, NitroPack and Hummingbird, whose settings it cannot read, it reminds you to keep only one of the two.

The same goes for loading scripts with defer: while Autoptimize, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Fastest Cache, Speed Optimizer, WP-Optimize or Jetpack Boost already defers your scripts, this plugin’s defer fix cannot be tried.

When a fix has nothing to do on your site, for example because your theme does not load that file in the first place, this plugin says “Nothing to gain” and leaves it off.

Safety

  • A fix is on only after it passed the test on your pages. There is no switch that skips the test.
  • Every page is tested twice, at the width of a desktop screen and at the width of a phone, because a stylesheet can hold rules that only apply on a phone.
  • The test also notices a script that stopped reacting to something still on the page, such as a button that looks the same but no longer adds a product to the cart.
  • While a fix is being tested, visitors do not see it. It is applied only to the test views.
  • “Turn off” puts everything back at once.
  • An emergency address, shown on the plugin’s screen, switches every fix off without logging in.
  • When a fix is switched on or off, this plugin clears the page cache so visitors do not keep getting the old pages.
  • Removing the plugin removes its settings, the picture copies and the minified copies it made.

What we tested it with

Themes: Astra, Kadence, GeneratePress, OceanWP, Twenty Twenty-Five, Hello Elementor with Elementor, Storefront.

Page caches, switching a fix on and off with the cache running: Cache Enabler, WP Super Cache, WP-Optimize, W3 Total Cache, Breeze, WP Fastest Cache.

This plugin also asks WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, Speed Optimizer, Hummingbird and Autoptimize to clear their cache, but we have not yet tested those ourselves. Other caches can listen to the speed_doctor_clear_cache action.

Privacy

This plugin sends nothing from your site anywhere. There is no account, no cloud service and no tracking. Everything it measures stays in your own database. The only link that leads away is one block on the plugin’s own screen, for people who would rather have the work done for them.

One fix fetches files from outside, and only when you start its test: “Serve Google Fonts from your own server” downloads the font stylesheets your pages already load from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) and the font files they name (fonts.gstatic.com) into your uploads folder. The request carries nothing about your site or visitors beyond what any browser sends for those files. Google Fonts terms: https://developers.google.com/fonts/terms · Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

The fix “Show YouTube videos as a picture until play is pressed” changes what visitors’ browsers load from YouTube, not whether they do: the page shows the video’s picture from YouTube’s image server (i.ytimg.com), and the YouTube player loads only when the visitor presses play. YouTube terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Site Check in the admin menu and press Check my site.
  3. Read the findings. Where a fix is available, press Fix it safely and keep the screen open until the test is done.
sections.faq:
Will it raise my PageSpeed Insights score?

It removes causes the score is built from, such as files a page does not use, the main picture loading late, pictures without a size and fonts from another server, and each fix shows what it saved on your pages. How much the score moves depends on what your site had to begin with, so this plugin makes no promise about the number.

Can someone fix my site for me?

Yes. The people behind this plugin fix slow WordPress and WooCommerce sites for a fixed price, on a copy of the site first, with a before-and-after measurement: imzura.com. The plugin works the same whether you ask or not.

Does it replace my cache plugin?

No. This plugin does not cache pages. Keep the cache plugin you have; this plugin clears its cache when a fix is switched on or off.

Another plugin already minifies my files. What happens?

This plugin reads that plugin’s setting, and while it is on, its own minify fix cannot be tried. The fix shows which plugin and which setting, with a link to its settings. Turn it off there, or keep that plugin and leave this plugin’s fix off.

Is minifying worth it if my server compresses files?

Less than without compression, and this plugin says so. The test measures what each fix saves on your own pages, and a fix that saves nothing is left off.

What happens if a fix breaks something?

It should not get that far: a fix that changes the text or the layout of a tested page, adds a script error or stops a file from loading is not kept. If you still see a problem, press “Turn off” next to the fix, or open the emergency address shown on the plugin’s screen. Both put the pages back as they were.

The test said “Not kept”. Is something wrong with my site?

No. It means the pages did not look exactly the same with the fix, so this plugin left it off. The reason is shown next to the fix.

I use W3 Total Cache and still see the old page right after switching a fix

In its “Disk: Enhanced” mode W3 Total Cache can keep serving a page for up to 30 seconds after the cache was cleared. Wait half a minute and reload.

The check or a test fails on a staging site locked with a server password

When a site sits behind HTTP Basic Auth, WordPress can mistake the lock’s user name and password for an application password and refuse the request. On the locked copy, switch application passwords off while you test:

add_filter( 'wp_is_application_passwords_available', '__return_false' );

I use reCAPTCHA v3 with Contact Form 7. Anything I should know?

With the Contact Form 7 fix on, the reCAPTCHA script loads only on pages that show a form. Google recommends running reCAPTCHA v3 on forms “as well as in the background of pages for analytics”. If you rely on v3 scores, weigh that before you keep the fix on.

Which WooCommerce files stay on every page?

The two scripts that record where a visitor came from. WooCommerce credits an order to the first page of the visit, and that is often a blog post or the homepage, so they are never removed. A stylesheet your theme has replaced with its own version is left alone as well: such a file also styles parts of the theme. On those themes the fix says “Nothing to gain”.

Why does this plugin not remove unused CSS?

Because nobody can know for sure which rules a site will never need. A rule unused on the pages a tool looks at may be needed on another page, by a menu or a form once a visitor taps it, or by a script that adds a class later; a site broken that way can look fine in every test. So this plugin tells you which stylesheets are the largest and who adds them, minifies them if you want, and leaves the rules alone.

How does this plugin time each plugin?

Only while the check reads a page or an admin screen, this plugin places a marker in WordPress’s hooks wherever the code passes from one plugin to another, and notes the time at each marker. A plugin’s time is what its own code took, without the time of the other plugins it called on the way; its database queries are those its code asked for, directly or through WordPress. Dashboard widgets are not run from a hook, so each one is timed on its own. The plugins themselves are not changed or wrapped, and the visits of real visitors are not measured. The time it takes to load a plugin’s files is not counted, so its real cost is a little higher than shown.

Which pictures does the picture fix leave alone?

Pictures WordPress already resizes for each screen (those with srcset), pictures set as a CSS background, and pictures on pages that were not opened during the test.

Does it work without WooCommerce?

Yes. The WooCommerce checks and the cart fix simply do not appear.
sections.changelog:
1.5.0

  • A new look for the plugin’s screen: the last check is summed up at the top, with a ring of the findings by level and the four counts, cards that show each finding’s level with a coloured strip and a label, plainer tabs, and a short explanation before the first check.
  • The summary of the check shows on the Check tab only, so the fix tabs start right below the title.
  • On a phone, the tables that show what a fix saved keep each number on one line and scroll sideways.

1.4.0

  • The check names hosting problems: PHP without OPcache, OPcache that is full, and slow pages where most of the server time passes outside every plugin and the theme, with the numbers for each page.
  • The check follows the same-site links on the pages it opens and names links that lead to a missing page (404 or 410) and links that go through redirects, with the whole chain.
  • After a check, the block at the bottom of the screen says how many findings are to fix first and worth fixing.

1.3.0

  • After a fix is kept, the plugin’s screen asks once, below the fixes, for a review on WordPress.org. “Do not ask again” hides it for good; nothing else on the admin changes.
  • The fix that keeps room for pictures leaves alone pictures marked sizes=”auto”. Browsers that support it, such as Chrome, already give them a fixed box, and writing a size into the tag changed how they look, so the trial did not keep the fix.
  • Add-ons can read what the check’s browser saw on each page (the speed_doctor_seen action), and the list of plugins that may already do a job names Perfect Images and Disable Media Sizes when they choose which picture sizes are made.
  • The fixes that change the finished page (WooCommerce files, heavy pictures, the main picture, Google Fonts, room for pictures, YouTube) use the page WordPress hands to plugins from 6.9 on, and need WordPress 6.9 or newer. The plugin opens no output buffer of its own across the page.
  • New fix: stop Heartbeat calls from visitors. When a plugin loads WordPress Heartbeat on public pages, every open tab calls admin-ajax.php again and again, past any page cache. Before the trial this plugin calls admin-ajax.php itself as a visitor and looks at what answers Heartbeat there; only when nothing does is the Heartbeat file left out, with a stand-in that keeps the scripts that asked for it working. Logged-in users keep Heartbeat.
  • Old revisions can be removed from the check’s report: all but the newest 5 of each post (or the number set in WP_POST_REVISIONS) go, autosaves stay. They are first written to a compressed copy in wp-content/uploads/imzura-site-check/copies, so “Put them back” restores the same rows and fields; “Delete the copy” removes it.
  • The check names Heartbeat loaded for visitors (how often it calls and who asks for it), admin screens where a plugin made Heartbeat call more often than every 60 seconds, and old revisions piling up in the database (how many, how much text, and the posts with the most).
  • New fix: serve Google Fonts from your own server. The trial counts the other websites each page connects to, among those both untouched views connected to; fewer is a gain and shows as a column in the table.
  • The check names the setting that keeps Google Fonts on your server in Astra, Kadence, OceanWP and Spectra, and GeneratePress font-display, when the fonts they load come from Google.
  • The check weighs what phones with 3× screens download next to 2× screens, from the srcset of each picture and the sizes of its files on the server. PageSpeed Insights tests phones at a lower density and does not show it.
  • The check counts the copies WordPress keeps of each picture (one per size the theme and plugins ask for) and the disk space they take, and names who added each size. It does not say which sizes to drop: pages pick sizes by screen width.
  • The check names a font that is loaded twice: asked from Google Fonts by two stylesheets (with the theme or plugin that likely adds each), or the same font file downloaded from two places.
  • The check also names animations on the first screen that never stop, and a font loaded for less than 3% of the text on pages where another font draws at least 10%.
  • New fix: keep room for pictures while they load. Pictures without a width and height get them from their file on the server; the trial counts such pictures on each page and shows the count in the table.
  • New fix: load the main picture of each page first. The trial counts a main picture that waits (lazy loading, or not marked urgent) and shows it in the table; a fix that makes the main picture wait is not kept.
  • The WooCommerce files fix now works on block themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five. WooCommerce adds its account link to the header of block themes, so every page counted as showing something from the store and the fix found nothing to leave out. The plain account link no longer counts; an account menu that opens still does.
  • The WooCommerce files fix also leaves out WooCommerce’s block stylesheet on pages without anything from the store.
  • The report keeps, for each page, which scripts and stylesheets it loaded, and the admin screen lets add-ons run a fix’s trial as its own button does.

1.2.0

  • The check now opens each page in a hidden frame, at phone width and as a first-time visitor, and reports what only a browser sees.
  • Errors on your pages, each put down to the plugin or theme it comes from: PHP errors while the page is built (a fatal error is named as such, with the pages it stops), script errors, and files that do not load.
  • Pictures: the largest picture on the first screen waiting for lazy loading or not marked as urgent, other lazy pictures on the first screen, pictures without a width and height, and layout shift with what moved the page.
  • Fonts: Google’s servers, many font files, text that waits for its font, Font Awesome loaded more than once, font preloads that cannot be used.
  • Scripts: files from other websites, the same library loaded twice, scripts that keep the browser busy; the largest stylesheets and scripts with the plugin or theme behind each.
  • Plugins that load their stylesheets on pages where none of their rules apply, and block styles on pages without blocks.
  • Plugins that keep the server busy: how long the code of each plugin and the theme ran while each page was built, and how many database queries it made. The table of plugins shows it for all of them. The same for the dashboard, the posts list and, with WooCommerce, the products and orders lists, opened as the administrator.
  • Speed settings that are off in Elementor, Formidable Forms and Wordfence, named as each plugin’s own screen names them.
  • A cache plugin that is active with its page caching switched off is named, with the setting. It no longer counts as a second cache next to the one in use (WP-Optimize kept for its database tools, for example).
  • Housekeeping: the PHP error log (public, large, who fills it), backup files in wp-content, the largest database tables, switched-off plugins, two SEO plugins at once.
  • The FAQ explains why this plugin minifies stylesheets but does not remove the parts a page does not use.

1.1.0

  • Minify scripts: a file that stops working once minified is now sent as it is, and the trial runs again without it, instead of the whole fix being turned off. The fix shows how many files are sent as they are.
  • Every fix now changes the page and its files in one pass, in a fixed order: files left out first, then the rest minified, then pictures and video players. Each fix works on what the fixes before it left, and a fix that fails leaves the page as the fixes before it made it.

1.0.0

  • New fixes: minify stylesheets, minify scripts, leave out the emoji script, load jQuery without jQuery Migrate, load scripts in the head with defer, show YouTube videos as a picture until play is pressed.
  • A trial now also counts the files a page waits for before it shows anything, and the embedded frames that load something.
  • A fix that does what another active optimizer already does cannot be tried; the screen names the plugin and the exact setting.
  • The check now looks at how the server delivers pages and files: compression and browser caching.
  • The same finding on several pages is now one finding that lists the pages.
  • The screen has tabs: Check, CSS & JS, Images, Plugins and Cache. The Cache tab shows the page cache in use, opens the home page as a new visitor, and clears the cache.
  • Fixed: from WordPress 6.7 every page logged a notice because the plugin’s texts were loaded too early.

0.8.0

  • Every page is now tested at phone width as well as at desktop width.

0.7.0

  • New fix: load WooCommerce files only on pages that show something from the store.
  • The test now notices a script that stopped reacting to something still on the page.
  • The check no longer counts the WooCommerce scripts that record where a visitor came from as unused.

0.6.1

  • Database reads use prepared table names.
  • Added this readme.

0.6.0

  • Switching a fix on or off, the emergency address and deactivating the plugin now clear the page cache.

0.5.0

  • New fix: serve heavy pictures at the size they are shown.

0.4.0

  • New in the check: what each plugin and the theme add to your pages.
  • Fixed: on block themes a form added by a template lost its stylesheet.

0.3.0

  • New fix: load Contact Form 7 only on pages that have a form.

0.2.0

  • The test engine: try a fix on hidden views, keep it only if the pages stay the same.
  • New fix: load the cart script only when the cart is in use.

0.1.0

  • The check and the admin screen.

  • Housekeeping: the PHP error log (whether strangers can download it, its size, the plugins that fill it), backup and archive files left in wp-content, the largest database tables, plugins that are installed but switched off, and two SEO plugins active at once
  • Settings WordPress loads on every request (autoloaded options) and the largest of them
  • Scheduled jobs that have fallen behind, including the Action Scheduler queue
  • WooCommerce: order storage, sessions that pile up, the cart script running outside the shop
  • The environment: PHP version, object cache, the page cache in use, and a cache plugin that is active with its page caching switched off (WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, Breeze, Hummingbird), named with the setting
  • How the server delivers pages and files: compressed (gzip, Brotli) or not, and whether browsers may keep stylesheets and scripts
  • The hosting: PHP running without OPcache, or with OPcache full, and slow pages whose time passes mostly outside the code of every plugin and the theme, which points at the server rather than at a plugin
  • Links: same-site links on the checked pages that lead to a missing page, and links that go through one or more redirects, each with the page it is on (up to 30 links per check, asked from your own server the way a visitor’s browser would)

The fixes

  • Load the cart script only when the cart is in use. WooCommerce asks the server for the header cart on every visitor’s first page view, even when the cart is empty. With the fix the empty cart comes with the page and the script loads the moment something is added. The cart and checkout pages are left as they are.
  • Load WooCommerce files only on pages that show something from the store. WooCommerce adds its stylesheets and scripts to every page of the site. With the fix a page that shows nothing from the store, no product, cart, notice or widget, is sent without them. Store pages and every page that shows a product keep all of them. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Load Contact Form 7 only on pages that have a form. Its script and stylesheet, and the reCAPTCHA or Turnstile script when one is connected, load only where a form is shown. Forms added by a template or placed with Elementor are covered.
  • Serve heavy pictures at the size they are shown. A JPEG or PNG far larger than the space it fills is replaced, for visitors, by a copy of the right size in WebP. The original stays in the media library untouched. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Load the main picture of each page first. The largest picture on the first screen is what Google times as the page’s Largest Contentful Paint. Some themes and page builders make it wait for lazy loading or leave it unmarked, so the browser fetches it last. The fix finds that picture on your pages as visitors see them and has the browser fetch it first; on posts and products whose main picture is the featured image, it does the same for every such page. Where WordPress already does this, the fix has nothing to do. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Serve Google Fonts from your own server. Fonts from Google make the browser connect to two more servers before text in them can show, and they pass each visitor’s IP address to Google. When you start its test, the fix downloads the fonts your pages load from Google into your uploads folder, adds font-display swap where it is missing, and points your pages at the copies. Fonts that a stylesheet pulls in with @import are left as they are. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Keep room for pictures while they load. A picture without a width and height in its tag takes no room until it arrives, and the text around it jumps when it does (Cumulative Layout Shift). The fix reads the size of each such picture from its file on your server and writes it into the tag. Pictures that load only when scrolled to get it once the test has seen them load; pictures from other websites are left as they are. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.
  • Minify stylesheets (CSS) and Minify scripts (JavaScript), two separate fixes. The spaces, line breaks and comments come out of your theme’s and plugins’ own files, and a smaller copy is sent instead, under the same handle. Files that are minified already, files from other sites and code written into the page are left alone, and so is a file that would not get at least 5% smaller. Addresses inside stylesheets are rewritten, so fonts and pictures still load. If a script stops working once minified, the trial sees the error in that file, sends it as it is from then on and tests again; the fix is kept only if the pages then work, and the screen shows how many files are sent as they are.
  • Leave out the emoji script. WordPress adds a script and styles to every page so that very old browsers can show emoji as pictures. Browsers in use today show emoji themselves.
  • Load jQuery without jQuery Migrate. Migrate only helps code written for old versions of jQuery. If a script on your site still needs it, the test sees it fail and the fix is not kept.
  • Load scripts in the head with defer. Scripts in the head of the page make the browser wait before it shows anything. With the fix they download alongside the page and run once it is read, in the same order as before. jQuery is left as it is, because code written into pages often needs it right away. Needs WordPress 6.3 or newer.
  • Show YouTube videos as a picture until play is pressed. An embedded YouTube video loads the whole player as soon as the page opens, even for visitors who never watch it. With the fix the video shows its picture, from YouTube, and a play button in the same place and size, and the player loads when the button is pressed. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.

The screen has a tab for each kind of fix (CSS & JS, Images, Plugins), one for the check, and one for your page cache: which one is active, a test that opens the home page as a new visitor, and a button that clears it.

Works with other optimizers

Two plugins minifying the same files is a common cause of broken pages. If Autoptimize, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Fastest Cache, W3 Total Cache, Speed Optimizer, WP-Optimize, Breeze, Jetpack Boost, Asset CleanUp or Fast Velocity Minify already minifies your stylesheets or scripts, this plugin does not try its own fix: it names the plugin and the exact setting, and links to that plugin’s settings. This plugin only reads their settings and never changes them. For WP Rocket, Perfmatters, FlyingPress, NitroPack and Hummingbird, whose settings it cannot read, it reminds you to keep only one of the two.

The same goes for loading scripts with defer: while Autoptimize, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Fastest Cache, Speed Optimizer, WP-Optimize or Jetpack Boost already defers your scripts, this plugin’s defer fix cannot be tried.

When a fix has nothing to do on your site, for example because your theme does not load that file in the first place, this plugin says “Nothing to gain” and leaves it off.

Safety

  • A fix is on only after it passed the test on your pages. There is no switch that skips the test.
  • Every page is tested twice, at the width of a desktop screen and at the width of a phone, because a stylesheet can hold rules that only apply on a phone.
  • The test also notices a script that stopped reacting to something still on the page, such as a button that looks the same but no longer adds a product to the cart.
  • While a fix is being tested, visitors do not see it. It is applied only to the test views.
  • “Turn off” puts everything back at once.
  • An emergency address, shown on the plugin’s screen, switches every fix off without logging in.
  • When a fix is switched on or off, this plugin clears the page cache so visitors do not keep getting the old pages.
  • Removing the plugin removes its settings, the picture copies and the minified copies it made.

What we tested it with

Themes: Astra, Kadence, GeneratePress, OceanWP, Twenty Twenty-Five, Hello Elementor with Elementor, Storefront.

Page caches, switching a fix on and off with the cache running: Cache Enabler, WP Super Cache, WP-Optimize, W3 Total Cache, Breeze, WP Fastest Cache.

This plugin also asks WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, Speed Optimizer, Hummingbird and Autoptimize to clear their cache, but we have not yet tested those ourselves. Other caches can listen to the speed_doctor_clear_cache action.

Privacy

This plugin sends nothing from your site anywhere. There is no account, no cloud service and no tracking. Everything it measures stays in your own database. The only link that leads away is one block on the plugin’s own screen, for people who would rather have the work done for them.

One fix fetches files from outside, and only when you start its test: “Serve Google Fonts from your own server” downloads the font stylesheets your pages already load from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) and the font files they name (fonts.gstatic.com) into your uploads folder. The request carries nothing about your site or visitors beyond what any browser sends for those files. Google Fonts terms: https://developers.google.com/fonts/terms · Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

The fix “Show YouTube videos as a picture until play is pressed” changes what visitors’ browsers load from YouTube, not whether they do: the page shows the video’s picture from YouTube’s image server (i.ytimg.com), and the YouTube player loads only when the visitor presses play. YouTube terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
